# 2026-11-21 CCS recheck: Summit/Polk County and ND amalgamation appeal

Search-level only (two searches, two article fetches). No primary court or IUC documents read.

- Polk County: Judge Beattie stayed the landowner/county/Sierra Club suit on 2025-12-23 (Yahoo/Register syndication, fetched) and sent the permit back to the IUC. The 2025-10 hearing article shows opponents called the amendment a "wholesale reboot" and the Farm Bureau questioned public purpose for eminent domain. All already captured as L001/L006. Nothing dated after the IUC July 2026 amendment turned up. The IUC "hazardous liquid pipeline requests" page shows "Updated October 7, 2026" but I could not see what changed. Docket numbers to check by hand: IUC HLP-2021-0001; Polk County CVCV067849 (from the search summary, not verified).
- ND amalgamation: a Bottineau County court held the pore-space amalgamation provision unconstitutional (taking without jury-determined just compensation), Dec 2025 (RFD-TV, Carbon Pulse; secondary). An appeal to the ND Supreme Court is "expected" but I found no report that one was filed or decided. No POET mention in any result.
- Net: no new leads. Both watchlist items pushed out rather than rechecked again.

Paper relevance: the amalgamation ruling is the strongest "eminent-domain/just-compensation" frame for Tier-type CCS comparison and should be coded as a distinct legitimacy dispute (property rights) from the Iowa permit fight (public purpose).
